verdict.rationale: Bun's package-manager CLI mirrors npm/yarn conventions. `bun install` is a drop-in for `npm install` in any Node.js project, alongside familiar verbs (add, remove, update, outdated, why, info, link, publish), the `-g/--global` and `--frozen-lockfile` flags, `bun pm pack` following npm pack rules, and npm `overrides`/Yarn `resolutions`/package.json workspaces. Community comments describe switching as near-zero cost. Missing for 10: an explicit command/flag-parity mapping for npm/yarn/pnpm users, documentation of where conventions diverge (e.g. lifecycle scripts not run by default), and independent hands-on confirmation of command-level familiarity.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can keep using familiar commands and interface conventions from the incumbent tool while adopting this manager

citations.quote: Switch from `npm install` to `bun install` in any Node.js project
`bun pm pack` creates a `.tgz` file containing all files that would be published to npm, following the same rules as `npm pack`.
Bun supports npm's `"overrides"` and Yarn's `"resolutions"` in `package.json`.
To install a package globally, use the `-g`/`--global` flag.
The `bun` CLI contains a Node.js-compatible package manager designed to be a dramatically faster replacement for `npm`, `yarn`, and `pnpm`.
Didn't prevent me from switching to Bun as the cost is 0.
